Working closely with the client, CGI colleagues and Service Design and Transition teams, you’ll ensure applications, data and capabilities move from on-premise infrastructure to cloud-based services in a controlled and sustainable way. You’ll translate business and technical requirements into effective service designs that support operational stability from transition through to live operation. You’ll bring together technical and business stakeholders, challenge assumptions constructively and identify opportunities to improve how services are designed and operated. With the support of a collaborative team, you’ll apply service management standards and governance while helping develop innovative approaches that improve resilience, efficiency and long-term service performance. Design & Deliver – Develop end-to-end service architectures and models aligned with business, operational and technical requirements. Migrate & Transition – Support the controlled migration of applications, data and capabilities from on-premise infrastructure into cloud environments. Govern & Assure – Ensure service designs and transitions adhere to agreed governance, architectural standards and service management processes. Manage & Mitigate – Identify service risks, issues and dependencies early and work collaboratively to develop effective mitigations. Improve & Innovate – Identify opportunities to improve service design, transition and operation through automation, modern tooling and new ways of working. Assure & Sustain – Ensure transitioned services are operationally ready, supportable and designed for long-term stability and continual improvement. Strong knowledge of service management frameworks such as ITIL 4, ISO/IEC 20000 or equivalent. Demonstrable experience supporting the migration of applications and data from on-premise to cloud environments, including SaaS, PaaS or IaaS. Deep understanding of the end-to-end service lifecycle, including design, transition, operation and continual improvement. Experience defining and managing SLAs, KPIs and service models, ideally within enterprise or government environments. Proven ability to engage and influence stakeholders while bridging business and technical perspectives. Experience operating within governed environments and applying enterprise service and architectural standards. Excellent communication, documentation and presentation skills. Knowledge of DevOps, automation and monitoring tooling for modern service environments is highly desirable. Understanding of cloud operations, ITSM tooling and CMDBs would be advantageous.

review_candidates.title: Senior Technical Lead - Leadership and Workforce Systems
review_candidates.description: Overview The Senior Technical Lead – Leadership & Workforce Systems provides strategic leadership, technical oversight, and quality assurance for the project's Human Resources for Health Leadership, Management, Governance and Regulation portfolio under RISE and ASCEND HRH activities. The position leads implementation of interventions that improve workforce planning, Human Resources (HR) management, leadership development, organizational performance, Human Resources for Health (HRH) information systems, digital innovation, monitoring and learning, implementation research, organizational strengthening, and institutional transition. The project supports the Government of Ethiopia to strengthen HRH systems, particularly in underserved and fragile settings where shortages of competent health workers, limited institutional capacity, and weak regulatory systems continue to affect access to quality primary health care. Working through national institutions and decentralized implementation platforms, the project advances sustainable, country-led HRH reforms that improve workforce competency, performance, resilience, and health system effectiveness. Working closely with the Ministry of Health (MOH), Regional Health Bureaus (RHB), Zonal Health Departments (ZHD), Civil Service Commission (CSC), universities, professional associations (PAs) and development partners, the Senior Technical Lead provides strategic directions to ensure project investments strengthen resilient HRH systems capable of sustaining long-term improvements in workforce performance, service delivery, and health system resilience. The position serves as Jhpiego's principal technical authority for this pillar, ensuring that all interventions are technically sound, evidence-based, innovative, well integrated, and aligned with Ethiopia's Human Resources for Health Strategic and Investment Plan, national regulatory frameworks, the America First Global Health Strategy (AFGHS), and other relevant national priorities. The Senior Technical Lead also promotes institutional capacity strengthening, country ownership, sustainability, adaptive management, and continuous technical innovation across the portfolio. Position is contingent on MOH and donor guidance. Responsibilities Strategic Technical Leadership Provide strategic leadership for all activities related to HRH leadership, governance, workforce planning, HR management, HRH information systems, digital HRH, organizational development, implementation science, Monitoring Evaluation and Learning (MEL) integration, knowledge management, institutional transition, and country ownership. Lead development and refinement of technical strategies that strengthen the Leadership Management and Governance (LMG) continuum for Ethiopia's health workforce. Identify, adapt, and promote global and national best practices that improve workforce planning, HR management, leadership development, organizational performance, HRH information systems, organizational strengthening, and institutional transition. Ensure all technical approaches are evidence-based, implementation-oriented, and responsive to Ethiopia's evolving HRH priorities. Guide annual technical planning, priority setting, resource allocation, and implementation sequencing across the project. Technical Oversight Lead implementation of leadership, workforce management, and governance strengthening, including leadership, workforce management, and professional regulation (systems strengthening components) Technically lead the implementation of data-driven HRH planning, learning and decision-making, including HRH information systems, evidence generation and use, and monitoring, learning and adaptive management Lead the implementation of institutional capacity and sustainability, including local partner organizational strengthening, institutional capacity, and transition and country ownership Ensure technical consistency across central, regional subnational and partner implementation teams. Coordinate closely with other Technical Leads to ensure seamless integration across all project objectives and avoid fragmented implementation. National Technical Leadership and Government Engagement Serve as Jhpiego's principal technical focal point for HRH Leadership and Workforce Systems with the MoH, RHBs, ZHDs, WoHOs, PHCUs, PAs, regulatory agencies, and development partners. Provide high-level technical assistance to national institutions in strengthening policies, standards, implementation frameworks, operational guidelines, and institutional systems. Lead or contribute to national technical working groups, advisory committees, policy dialogues, and strategic planning processes. Cultivate and maintain productive working relationships with government counterparts and development partners to promote harmonization, institutional ownership, and sustainability. Ensure project investments strengthen—not duplicate—existing national systems and government priorities. Technical Quality Assurance Ensure all technical interventions meet national standards, international best practices, and donor expectations. Lead development and quality assurance of HRH policies, leadership frameworks, workforce planning tools, HR dashboards, digital platforms, organizational assessment tools, transition roadmaps, MEL frameworks, and evidence-generation strategies. Review and approve major technical deliverables before dissemination. Ensure interventions remain technically sound, operationally feasible, and responsive to emerging national priorities. Innovation and Technical Advancement Provide technical leadership on integrated Human Resources Information System (iHRIS), interoperability, workforce intelligence, AI-supported analytics, dashboards, HR analytics, digital governance, and decision-support systems Monitor emerging global evidence and identify innovations appropriate for adaptation within Ethiopia. Promote implementation of science and continuous improvement across technical interventions. Institutional Capacity Strengthening and Technical Mentorship Strengthen institutional capacity of government agencies, higher education institutions, regulatory bodies, professional associations, and teaching hospitals to independently sustain HRH reforms. Provide high-level technical mentoring and coaching to Senior Advisors, Sub-national technical team, government counterparts, and partner organizations. Support development of national technical expertise and succession planning. Foster multidisciplinary collaboration and strengthen communities of practice that promote continuous learning and technical excellence. Technical Integration and Systems Strengthening Ensure seamless integration among competency-based education, accreditation, Continuous Professional Development (CPD), competency assessment, licensing, professional regulation, HRH digital systems, quality improvement, workforce planning, and evidence generation. Coordinate closely with the Senior Technical Lead – Development & Regulation to maximize technical synergies across project objectives. Promote integrated implementation approaches that strengthen institutional systems rather than isolated interventions. Ensure interventions contribute to sustainable health systems strengthening and long-term government ownership. Monitoring, Learning and Adaptive Management Use program data, implementation evidence, and routine monitoring findings to assess technical performance and implementation quality. Identify implementation successes, challenges, risks, bottlenecks, and emerging opportunities. Recommend corrective actions and technical adaptations that improve program effectiveness. Support adaptive management through regular technical reviews, learning sessions, after-action reviews, and performance reflection meetings. Work closely with the MEL team to strengthen evidence generation and utilization for continuous improvement. Knowledge Management, Research, and Business Development Lead development of technical briefs, implementation guides, policy briefs, technical reports, success stories, case studies, conference abstracts, peer-reviewed publications, and other knowledge products. Promote documentation and dissemination of innovations, lessons learned, and best practices nationally and internationally. Foster organizational learning and strengthen technical communities of practice across project partners. Identify opportunities for strategic partnerships, leveraged investments, and future HRH programming. Contribute technical expertise to proposal development, concept notes, strategic planning, and organizational business development initiatives as requested. Representation Represent Jhpiego in national and international technical working groups, conferences, scientific meetings, donor consultations, academic forums, regulatory meetings, and professional networks. Present technical achievements, innovations, research findings, and lessons learned through conferences, publications, and policy dialogues. Strengthen Jhpiego's reputation as a national and global leader in HRH systems strengthening. Cross-Cutting Responsibilities Promote country ownership, institutional strengthening, localization, sustainability, and transition planning across all interventions. Ensure integration of safeguarding, ethics, digital transformation, quality improvement, and knowledge management throughout the technical portfolio. review_candidates.description: Job Description Introduction Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants. IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration Applications are welcome from internal and external candidates. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. For the purpose of this vacancy, internal and internal-equivalent candidates as well as external women candidates are considered as first-tier candidates. Organizational Context and Scope IOM Ireland has been operating in Ireland since 2001, currently in following areas of migration management: Assisted Voluntary Return and Reintegration, Resettlement, Family Reunification, Counter-Trafficking, Protection, Integration Support to Beneficiaries of Temporary Protection, Immigration and Border Governance (IBG) and Mental Health and Psychosocial Support. Within its IBG and Protection services, IOM Ireland provides support to international protection applicants in Ireland and beneficiaries of temporary protection during their application and/or registration process mainly through provision of cultural mediation and case work assistance. The Unit also supports counter-trafficking efforts in Ireland. Under the direct supervision of the Chief of Mission, and in collaboration with the relevant units at Headquarters, Regional and Sub-regional offices, the incumbent will be accountable and responsible for the management of the Immigration, Border Governance and Protection Unit projects in maintaining close collaboration with donors other partners and different stakeholders. The position will oversee the coordination and implementation of all project activities from development, roll-out and regular operational aspects of the project in multiple sites. Responsibilities Coordinate the overall implementation of the IBG and Protection projects in Ireland including the oversight of the financial, logistical, administrative and technical aspects in accordance with IOM’s policies, practices and global standards as well as relevant requirements, guidelines and donors agreements. Monitor projects implementation according to the work plans; document and evaluate results; identify the causes of deviations and bottlenecks and recommend and implement timely corrective actions in coordination with COM. Promote and contribute to the integration and mainstreaming of gender, protection, human rights and other pertinent cross-cutting issues into projects implementation. Develop monitoring, evaluation, and reporting tools for the IBG and Protection projects. Contribute to information management including awareness raising and visibility, press releases, website updates and other relevant information-sharing materials. Identify potential areas for project development and contribute to the development of new projects by selecting and summarizing background information, assessing the local context and drafting segments of project proposals. Actively participate in the mission´s Senior Management Team to contribute to proper synergies within the mission as well as to the early identification of opportunities for IOM in Ireland. Participate in the development of new projects and identify potential synergies among thematic areas of the mission. Participate in the development and adjustment of methodologies, contingency plans, approaches and standard operations procedures to respond to emerging challenges in Ireland through a consultative process with other relevant parties in the office. Coordinate the elaboration and dissemination of reports for donors, government and other relevant stakeholders ensuring timely submission and compliance with donor and IOM requirements. Liaise and coordinate with government entities, implementing partners, United Nation agencies, civil society, donors and other stakeholders. Plan, develop, organize and deliver capacity building activities to build capacity of staff, partners, government officials, and other humanitarian actors. Participate in relevant conferences, working groups, workshops, steering committees, working groups, consultations and other forums as required. Supervise IBG Unit team to ensure productivity and adherence to IOM rules and regulations. Initiate and actively support timely selection and recruitment of the project team members as needed; ensure proper onboarding and continuous training and development of the IBG and Protection staff. Evaluate individual and overall performance of the staff under his/her supervision. Ensure all IBG and Protection team members receive tools needed to perform their tasks as required. Provide the overall IBG Unit team supervision, management and guidance in terms of productivity, performance and adherence to IBG rules, regulations and relevant SOPs; Undertake duty travel as required. Perform other duties as may assigned by Chief of Mission. Qualifications Required Qualifications and Experience Education Bachelor’s degree in political or social sciences, International Relations, Development Studies, Migration Studies, Human Rights, Law or related fields from an accredited academic institution with four years of relevant professional experience; or, Master’s degree in the above-mentioned fields with two years of relevant professional experience; Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database. Experience Experience in liaising with governmental authorities, national/international institutions, United Nations agencies and non-governmental organizations; Experience in project management with yearly budget over EUR 2 million; Experience with leading multinational team exceeding 12 persons; Experience in working with migrants, refugees, internally displaced persons, victims of trafficking or other vulnerable groups; Prior work experience with provision of the IBG is an advantage; and, Prior work experience with international humanitarian organizations, non-government or government institutions/organization in a multi-cultural setting is an advantage. Skills In depth knowledge of the broad range of immigration policies and regulations; Knowledge of the Irish asylum system; Knowledge of UN and bilateral donor programming; and, Knowledge of UN financial, administrative and human resources rules and regulations. Languages All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish). For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written). Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments. Required Competencies IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link . Competencies will be assessed during the selection process. Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values: Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion. Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct. Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges. Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance. Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated. Core Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2 Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results. Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes. Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate. Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work. Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way. Managerial Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 2, if with direct reports Leadership: Provides a clear sense of direction, leads by example and demonstrates the ability to carry out the Organization’s vision. Assists others to realize and develop their leadership and professional potential. Empowering others: Creates an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential. Building Trust: Promotes shared values and creates an atmosphere of trust and honesty. Strategic thinking and vision: Works strategically to realize the Organization’s goals and communicates a clear strategic direction. Humility: Leads with humility and shows openness to acknowledging own shortcomings. Notes Please refer to this link for guidance on IOM Job Category. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months. This post is subject to local recruitment. Only persons holding a valid residence and work permit in Ireland will be eligible for consideration.
